correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple graph, F²(x)=x forces two-step firing sums into the Laplacian kernel; primitive two-cycles consequently use complementary firing vectors. Solving inequalities at each vertex gives c_v independent chip counts in explicit intervals, with exact total-energy generating product z^(2m-|cut|)prod_v[c_v]_z. Each unoriented cut corresponds to the two states of each orbit. Positivity and the local optimality of maximum cuts prove both extreme energies and their maximum-cut multiplicities. The tree recurrence and Pell formula follow from independent edge selections. NP-completeness is reduced from connected MAX-CUT. Independent standard-library verification checked 72 graphs and 1,821,396 confined states, plus 21 tree-recursion and 14 Pell evaluations; finite tests corroborate rather than replace the general proof.

originality.rationale: No identified primary or prior record implies the energy-resolved period-two orbit enumerator for every connected simple graph. Jiang (2010) gives equal firing counts, Jiang–Scully–Zhang (2012/2015) gives allowed firing patterns, and Bitar–Goles (1992) establishes periods on trees; the present cut-degree polynomial, MAX-CUT edge support and path Pell evaluation are additional quantified conclusions. Historical equivalence remains a stated risk because the 1992 full text was unavailable.
residual_risks: The full text of Bitar–Goles (1992), the most plausible earlier tree source, could not be inspected; its abstract alone does not justify a whole-document noncoverage claim.
The newest middle-stair paper was compared through public theorem statements, not an exhaustive full-text audit; an unobserved independent argument for the cut enumerator remains possible.
Search ranking and source access cannot prove bibliographic uniqueness; unindexed historical enumerations may exist.

value.rationale: Exact energy-resolved recurrent orbit counts are natural conserved-energy invariants of the fixed-energy sandpile. The theorem identifies their support endpoints with graph MAX-CUT, counts extremal orbits via the number of maximum cuts, and proves NP-completeness of low-energy period-two existence. It also gives a uniform tree recursion and closed Pell path census, going beyond prior possible-period and firing-pattern classifications. The combination is a substantive structural all-graph classification, not a selected small-table recomputation.
